requirementSpec.intent: Build a polished Roblox main menu titled AURORA. Features: Play, Settings, Credits. Settings opens a panel with Music on/off toggle and Volume slider. Credits opens a small panel. Both panels have Close. Desktop and mobile. Rich glossy cyan/cobalt artwork with thick navy edges, warm gold highlights, ornamental corner details and a title plate. Use Gemini-generated matching skins and icons: button skins, panel skin, slider track and handle, toggle on/off pieces and distinct play/settings/credits/close icons. Keep text live and readable. Create only these features; no shop, rewards, currency, ranks or invented game systems. Play closes the menu and fires a clearly named local hook for game integration. Coherent hover and press animation. Native background layout with restrained decoration. Panels must open and close in the actual controller.

designPlan.artDirection: Premium fantasy-tech menu with a restrained native backdrop and concentrated glossy artwork on the foreground controls. The visual identity is built from luminous cyan and deep cobalt enamel surfaces framed by thick navy edges, kissed with warm gold trims and selective specular streaks. The centerpiece is an ornate title plate carrying live AURORA lettering, with menu buttons stacked beneath as a ceremonial command column. Settings and Credits appear as compact modal cards using the same skin family, with understated ornamental corners repeated only at the screen frame extremities and title framing so the background never competes with the main actions. All text remains crisp live Roblox text over darker interior fills for readability; artwork is reserved for skins, plates, slider parts, toggle states, icons, and corner ornaments.

composition.focalPoint: The dominant focal point is the Play button centered beneath the AURORA title plate, forming a single vertical hero axis. Settings and Credits are subordinate peers in the same dock directly attached to the Play action so the interface reads as one cohesive command stack rather than scattered buttons. Secondary focus shifts to the currently open modal panel, which overlays the dock while keeping the title context visible behind it.
secondaryRegions: background_frame for restrained native atmospheric fill and corner ornaments
settings_modal for Music toggle, Volume slider, and Close
credits_modal for compact credits information and Close
composition.alignmentSystem: Use a centered axial composition. Title plate, title text, and the menu dock share one vertical centerline. Modal windows also center on the same axis to preserve continuity between the menu and overlays. Internal panel content aligns to a clean left text column with right-side controls for settings rows. Decorative corner elements pin to safe-area corners and never disturb control alignment.

visualSystem.colorRationale: Primary cyan drives interactive emphasis and glossy energy, while cobalt provides depth and secondary body color within the same cool family. Thick navy outlines stabilize the ornate artwork and keep it readable against the background. Warm gold is used sparingly for trims, title accents, and highlight moments so the screen feels premium without becoming noisy. Neutral surfaces stay dark and desaturated to let live white text and cyan controls pop consistently.
visualSystem.outlineStyle: Foreground skins use thick navy perimeter strokes with lighter inner cyan highlights. Buttons and panels receive a double-read edge: dark outer border for silhouette plus narrow gold or pale cyan inner gleam depending on hierarchy. Live text is not heavily outlined; use subtle contrast support via dark plate interiors and occasional soft shadow only.
visualSystem.shadowStyle: Short, dense navy shadows under all major foreground components with slightly deeper lift on the primary Play CTA and modal windows. Shadows should feel glossy and premium rather than soft-floating: low spread, medium opacity, directional downward bias, and a faint ambient cyan bloom on highlighted surfaces.

iconSystem.styleDescription: Gemini-generated icon family with front-facing embossed silhouettes nested into glossy cyan/cobalt medallion logic, outlined in deep navy and touched with warm gold accents. Icons should feel handcrafted to the same artwork kit as the button skins rather than flat stock glyphs.

motionSystem.hover: Pointer-capable devices use restrained premium motion: buttons and close controls rise 2-3%, gain a focused specular sweep, and slightly intensify cyan and gold highlights. Slider handle lifts subtly on hover; toggle shell brightens.
motionSystem.press: All actionable controls use tactile compression with shortened shadows and a slight darkening of lower edges. Toggle includes a quick state pulse; slider handle compresses at drag start; Play gets the strongest but still controlled response.
motionSystem.entrance: Menu content fades and rises in together as a single composition, with title plate first, then Play, then secondary buttons in quick succession. Modals fade and scale from 96% to 100% while dimming attention behind them only through layering, not a heavy overlay.
motionSystem.release: Controls spring back quickly to resting state with no exaggerated bounce. Modals close through a short fade/scale-down and visibility toggle managed by controller state.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: When reduced motion is preferred, disable scale shifts and specular sweeps; keep only quick opacity and color-state changes so hierarchy and feedback remain clear.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and drag responses only. No hover effects are synthesized. Press states trigger immediately on touch-down for buttons, toggles, and slider handle, then settle on release.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI sounds on touch or pointer because sounds were not requested.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a sound layer exists globally, this screen does not claim it as part of the design; unresolved or absent sounds are treated as intentional silence.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: Build _NexusDesktop as the initially visible group. Desktop centers the menu in a ceremonial vertical stack with broad breathing room, larger title plate span, and compact modal overlays that do not consume the whole screen. Button widths are content-dominant rather than full-screen, with Play clearly taller than Settings and Credits. Keep background decoration subtle and peripheral.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: Build _NexusMobile alongside desktop and switch at runtime when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) < 600. Mobile reflows into a narrower centered stack with full-width touch-friendly buttons, reduced ornament scale, and modals widened to safe margins. Simplify spacing density, preserve title-first then Play-first hierarchy, and enlarge all actionable controls to at least 48px touch targets. Do not simply scale desktop; tighten vertical composition and protect gesture/notch zones.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Tablet keeps the centered axial composition but uses an intermediate density between desktop and phone_portrait. Buttons can remain wider than phone while preserving bigger touch targets. Modals stay centered and moderately compact rather than full-width. Ornament scale may be slightly richer than phone but still restrained.

implementationNotes: Create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile Frame groups at View.build() return, each containing the same canonical nodeName set where visual nodes exist; desktop visible initially.

Use the exact supported node names from the library template: BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, TitlePlate, AuroraTitle, PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, SettingsModal, SettingsTitle, SettingsCloseButton, MusicRow, MusicLabel, MusicToggle, VolumeRow, VolumeLabel, VolumeSlider, VolumeValue, CreditsModal, CreditsTitle, CreditsBody, CreditsCloseButton, OnPlayRequestedHook, PanelControllerBehavior.
Do not add other visual controls, tabs, counters, currencies, shops, ranks, rewards, inventories, or extra navigation.
Keep all requested labels as live Roblox text; artwork is only for skins, title plate, icons, slider parts, toggle states, and corner ornaments.

Use a shared local helper in View for repeated skin/image/text setup and layout construction; use shared ButtonEffects module for hover/press behaviors across buttons, close buttons, toggle, and slider handle interactions.
SettingsButton opens SettingsModal and ensures CreditsModal is closed; CreditsButton opens CreditsModal and ensures SettingsModal is closed.
SettingsCloseButton closes SettingsModal. CreditsCloseButton closes CreditsModal. PanelControllerBehavior owns these state transitions in the actual controller.
PlayButton closes the menu root and then triggers OnPlayRequestedHook as a clearly named local integration callback/event contract for game startup.
MusicToggle must expose on/off visual states using generated matching toggle artwork pieces; VolumeSlider must use generated matching track and handle artwork pieces with actual draggable behavior.

Use UIListLayout, UIPadding, UITextSizeConstraint, UIScale, UIStroke, UICorner, UIAspectRatioConstraint, and CanvasGroup where appropriate. Preserve aspect ratio on title plate, corner ornaments, and fixed-art slider/toggle elements.
No audio assets should be claimed or fabricated. If a generic sound layer exists elsewhere, this screen still reports no requested audio satisfied here.
Modal visuals should be initially hidden and only shown via controller state; all instances must still exist at build time.
Distinct generated icons are required for Play, Settings, Credits, and Close, all in the same aurora_gloss_icons family with matching weight and treatment.

iconSystem.styleDescription: Gemini-generated icon family with front-facing embossed silhouettes nested into glossy cyan/cobalt medallion logic, outlined in deep navy and touched with warm gold accents. Icons should feel handcrafted to the same artwork kit as the button skins rather than flat stock glyphs.

motionSystem.hover: Pointer-capable devices use restrained premium motion: buttons and close controls rise 2-3%, gain a focused specular sweep, and slightly intensify cyan and gold highlights. Slider handle lifts subtly on hover; toggle shell brightens.
motionSystem.press: All actionable controls use tactile compression with shortened shadows and a slight darkening of lower edges. Toggle includes a quick state pulse; slider handle compresses at drag start; Play gets the strongest but still controlled response.
motionSystem.entrance: Menu content fades and rises in together as a single composition, with title plate first, then Play, then secondary buttons in quick succession. Modals fade and scale from 96% to 100% while dimming attention behind them only through layering, not a heavy overlay.
motionSystem.release: Controls spring back quickly to resting state with no exaggerated bounce. Modals close through a short fade/scale-down and visibility toggle managed by controller state.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: When reduced motion is preferred, disable scale shifts and specular sweeps; keep only quick opacity and color-state changes so hierarchy and feedback remain clear.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and drag responses only. No hover effects are synthesized. Press states trigger immediately on touch-down for buttons, toggles, and slider handle, then settle on release.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI sounds on touch or pointer because sounds were not requested.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a sound layer exists globally, this screen does not claim it as part of the design; unresolved or absent sounds are treated as intentional silence.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: Build _NexusDesktop as the initially visible group. Desktop centers the menu in a ceremonial vertical stack with broad breathing room, larger title plate span, and compact modal overlays that do not consume the whole screen. Button widths are content-dominant rather than full-screen, with Play clearly taller than Settings and Credits. Keep background decoration subtle and peripheral.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: Build _NexusMobile alongside desktop and switch at runtime when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) < 600. Mobile reflows into a narrower centered stack with full-width touch-friendly buttons, reduced ornament scale, and modals widened to safe margins. Simplify spacing density, preserve title-first then Play-first hierarchy, and enlarge all actionable controls to at least 48px touch targets. Do not simply scale desktop; tighten vertical composition and protect gesture/notch zones.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Tablet keeps the centered axial composition but uses an intermediate density between desktop and phone_portrait. Buttons can remain wider than phone while preserving bigger touch targets. Modals stay centered and moderately compact rather than full-width. Ornament scale may be slightly richer than phone but still restrained.

implementationNotes: Create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile Frame groups at View.build() return, each containing the same canonical nodeName set where visual nodes exist; desktop visible initially.

Use the exact supported node names from the library template: BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, TitlePlate, AuroraTitle, PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, SettingsModal, SettingsTitle, SettingsCloseButton, MusicRow, MusicLabel, MusicToggle, VolumeRow, VolumeLabel, VolumeSlider, VolumeValue, CreditsModal, CreditsTitle, CreditsBody, CreditsCloseButton, OnPlayRequestedHook, PanelControllerBehavior.
Do not add other visual controls, tabs, counters, currencies, shops, ranks, rewards, inventories, or extra navigation.
Keep all requested labels as live Roblox text; artwork is only for skins, title plate, icons, slider parts, toggle states, and corner ornaments.

Use a shared local helper in View for repeated skin/image/text setup and layout construction; use shared ButtonEffects module for hover/press behaviors across buttons, close buttons, toggle, and slider handle interactions.
SettingsButton opens SettingsModal and ensures CreditsModal is closed; CreditsButton opens CreditsModal and ensures SettingsModal is closed.
SettingsCloseButton closes SettingsModal. CreditsCloseButton closes CreditsModal. PanelControllerBehavior owns these state transitions in the actual controller.
PlayButton closes the menu root and then triggers OnPlayRequestedHook as a clearly named local integration callback/event contract for game startup.
MusicToggle must expose on/off visual states using generated matching toggle artwork pieces; VolumeSlider must use generated matching track and handle artwork pieces with actual draggable behavior.

Use UIListLayout, UIPadding, UITextSizeConstraint, UIScale, UIStroke, UICorner, UIAspectRatioConstraint, and CanvasGroup where appropriate. Preserve aspect ratio on title plate, corner ornaments, and fixed-art slider/toggle elements.
No audio assets should be claimed or fabricated. If a generic sound layer exists elsewhere, this screen still reports no requested audio satisfied here.
Modal visuals should be initially hidden and only shown via controller state; all instances must still exist at build time.
Distinct generated icons are required for Play, Settings, Credits, and Close, all in the same aurora_gloss_icons family with matching weight and treatment.

changeInstructions: Create a main menu titled AURORA.
Include only Play, Settings, and Credits as main actions.
Make Settings open a panel containing a Music on/off toggle and Volume slider.
Make Credits open a small panel.
Provide Close actions for both panels.
Play must close the menu and fire a clearly named local hook for game integration.
Implement coherent hover and press animation.
Support desktop and mobile layouts.
Use rich glossy cyan/cobalt artwork with thick navy edges, warm gold highlights, ornamental corner details, and a title plate.
Use Gemini-generated matching skins and icons.
Keep text live and readable.
Use a native background layout with restrained decoration.
Panels must open and close in the actual controller.
